tasks.short: Explain HR policies and employment rules to employees and managers.

steps.what: Receive the question and establish the employee's circumstances.
Find current policies, relevant agreements and authoritative employment guidance.
Interpret the sources and draft an explanation for the employee's circumstances.

loop.input: Scoped question and approved source passages with jurisdiction, version and effective date.
loop.output: Draft explanation with passage citations, assumptions and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require citations for substantive claims; verify source versions and flag conflicting or missing authority.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unresolved issues go to the HR specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Questions describe circumstances in free text and require explanations across several policy passages.

steps.what: Check interpretation, resolve exceptions and approve the answer.
Explain the answer and discuss practical consequences with the employee or manager.
Record advice and follow-up actions in the restricted case record.

tasks.design: Configure structured question intake in the {WORKFLOW} and retrieve versioned sources from the {DOCS} using jurisdiction and topic filters. A bounded loop drafts cited explanations; the HR specialist approves advice and handles consequential conversations. An integration stores the approved answer and agreed actions in the {HCM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policies, agreements and legal guidance have different versions and scopes. Search alone does not explain how they fit an employee's circumstances.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing intake and search functions cover much of the work. AI coding reduces the effort of connecting them, while bounded drafting can turn approved passages into a reviewable explanation.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting agreements, disputed facts and sensitive employment consequences still require judgement. Source permissions and version maintenance need continuing attention.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a technically correct answer misses a fairness concern, a personal difficulty or a developing dispute.

ambition.what: A manager clinic for upcoming leave and flexible-work decisions.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repeated source searches to exception advice and manager coaching. The specialist can recommend preventative action earlier; authority to change policy does not automatically increase.

reach.task: Assess whether an individual policy question signals a collective agreement dispute.
reach.learn: Agreement hierarchy, consultation routes and early dispute assessment.

build_days.consent_and_access: 10-30; 20-45 if employee consultation is required under national rules

evidence.claim: Structured intake, versioned retrieval and record updates are established deterministic patterns; this design is an estimate.
The digest provides no documented HR policy-answering case establishing accuracy or time savings.
GDPR data minimisation and access controls apply to employee questions and advice records.

assumptions: Typical work mixes document research, written answers and conversations; the mail share is not treated as a fixed measurement.
An approved policy library can be indexed by topic, jurisdiction and effective date.
The source pack is a retrieval result, not a guarantee that every relevant legal source was found.
Routine procedural questions need less discussion than the blended conversation estimate.
All time shares, remaining-time percentages and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Which jurisdictions, collective agreements and local policies apply.
Whether the policy library has reliable owners and version history.
Where sensitive HR case records are currently stored.
Which advice requires legal counsel or HR manager approval.
Which access, consultation and data-protection assessments are required.
research_questions: How often do historical questions require sources outside the approved library?
Can retrieval and drafting reliably detect expired policies and conflicting agreements?
Which recurring questions can be answered by an existing approved explanation?
new_work: Review cited drafts and investigate conflicting sources.
Maintain policy metadata and withdraw superseded guidance.
Sample answers for unsupported claims and inappropriate disclosure.
Route sensitive exceptions to the right adviser.

tasks.short: Confirm hiring terms, issue employment documents and complete starter administration.

steps.what: Confirm the selected candidate, approved vacancy and proposed employment terms.
Provide starter details and required supporting documents.
Check completeness and prepare the contract from approved templates.
Approve hiring terms and resolve exceptions within delegated authority.
Discuss the offer with the candidate and address questions about terms.
Send the approved contract for signature.
Review and sign the employment contract.
Create the employee record and notify teams responsible for the start.

tasks.design: Configure starter forms and approval routing in the {ATS} and {WORKFLOW}, with deterministic contract generation from approved templates in the {DOCS}. Release through the {ESIGN} follows approval of the exact contract version; signature completion triggers validated updates to the {HCM} and {PAYROLL}. People retain selection, negotiation, exception approval and signing decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Candidate details, approved terms and employee records are held in different places. Template variations and repeated entry make a single reliable handoff difficult.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, templates, approval routing and signature events cover most steps. AI-assisted development makes the remaining field mappings and validation rules cheaper to implement.
tasks.still_hard: Non-standard terms, identity and work-authorisation exceptions, cross-border employment and payroll cutoffs still need specialist handling.
tasks.human_edge: Explain the employment bargain clearly, negotiate within authority and recognise when a candidate's concern needs a real conversation.

ambition.what: A pre-start readiness check for candidates with cross-border employment arrangements.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time copying details and more time resolving terms and start-date risks. They can coordinate a readiness recommendation; hiring and pay exceptions retain their existing approval rights.

reach.task: Validate starter information before the first payroll cutoff.
reach.learn: Required payroll fields, effective dates and reconciliation of starter records.

reach.role: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialist
reach.task: Check proposed offers against the pay framework.
reach.learn: Job levels, pay ranges and evidence required for an exception.

build_days.consent_and_access: 10-30; 20-45 where national rules require employee consultation

evidence.claim: Template generation, approval routing, signature events and starter integrations are established deterministic capabilities.
Recruitment and selection AI can fall within the EU AI Act's high-risk employment category; administrative automation requires separate scoping.
The digest contains no documented case establishing savings for this hiring-paperwork design.

assumptions: The task starts with a selection decision; assessment and interviewing are separate activities.
The hiring manager has delegated approval authority for standard offers.
Candidate time is included because candidate actions form part of the task; it is not HR time saved.
Changed terms return to approval before another contract is released.
No model loop is needed for standard structured starter data and approved contract templates.
All time shares, remaining-time percentages and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Actual offer approval limits and contract variants.
Which integrations and signature events are available.
Which starter checks require inspection by an authorised person.
Whether candidates already use a secure starter form.
Applicable national employment and consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which standard fields are entered more than once between selection and first payroll?
Which contract exceptions account for most rework?
Can signature callbacks be retried safely without creating duplicate employee records?
new_work: Resolve failed validations and incomplete starter submissions.
Maintain contract templates and approval limits.
Reconcile signature completion with employee and payroll records.
Monitor failed handoffs and duplicate records.
Reapprove contracts when negotiated terms change.

tasks.short: Keep current on EU and national equality, disability and non-discrimination requirements.

steps.what: Check official updates and subscribed employment-law alerts.
Read changes and compare them with existing equality guidance.

loop.input: Approved legal source texts, prior versions and existing equality guidance.
loop.output: Cited change brief identifying jurisdiction, legal status, dates and affected topics.
loop.check: Verify quotations and dates against originals; distinguish proposals, enacted rules and judgments.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt per update; incomplete comparisons return to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Legal changes and their explanations arrive as varied prose rather than consistent structured amendments.

steps.what: Assess applicability and identify affected hiring or employment practices.
Resolve uncertain interpretations with legal counsel or the equality officer.
Draft updates to internal guidance and the compliance action list.

loop.input: Validated interpretation, existing guidance and identified process impacts.
loop.output: Tracked guidance changes and proposed actions linked to source passages.
loop.check: Compare each substantive change with the validated interpretation; require owners and dates for actions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved wording goes to the HR specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Changes require contextual edits to prose; fixed templates cannot reliably express every amendment.

steps.what: Approve guidance changes and assign compliance actions.

tasks.design: Configure official-source alerts and a deduplicated update queue in the {WORKFLOW}. Bounded loops compare source texts and draft changes in the {DOCS}, while the specialist assesses applicability and consults legal counsel. Approved guidance versions link to assigned actions in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding updates is straightforward; identifying their practical effect across jurisdictions and agreements is not. Summaries often omit qualifications needed for employment decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Source monitoring and version comparison already exist. Bounded extraction and drafting reduce reading and editing effort when the underlying texts remain available for checking.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding precedent, reasonable accommodation and indirect discrimination requires sustained learning. National rules and collective agreements prevent a universal compliance answer.
tasks.human_edge: Understand why a rule exists and spot employment practices that create unequal outcomes despite apparently neutral wording.

ambition.what: A quarterly accessibility and equality review of recruitment forms.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time collecting alerts and more time studying consequential changes and testing their practical effect. They gain capacity to recommend process changes; formal policy approval stays with the HR manager.

reach.task: Review recruitment procedures for accessibility and unequal treatment.
reach.learn: Accommodation assessment, indirect discrimination and evidence for proportionate process changes.

reach.task: Turn approved equality guidance into manager learning material.
reach.learn: Scenario design and checks that managers understand the changed requirement.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-10; 15-30 if subsequent process changes require national consultation

evidence.claim: Official-source monitoring, version comparison and action tracking can use deterministic technology.
Bounded legal-text summarisation still requires source checks and qualified interpretation.
The digest contains no documented case showing reliable automated maintenance of employment-law knowledge.

assumptions: The task is translated to EU and applicable national equality and disability requirements.
The specialist uses public legal sources without processing individual employee cases in the monitoring loop.
Legal counsel is consulted for uncertain changes, rather than every update.
The specialist continues reading selected primary sources to maintain professional understanding.
All time shares, remaining-time percentages and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Countries, workforce groups and collective agreements in scope.
Current source subscriptions and rights to store their content.
Availability of legal counsel and equality expertise.
Who approves guidance and resulting process changes.
Whether any planned change triggers consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which authoritative sources cover each applicable jurisdiction?
Can the comparison distinguish a proposal from a rule already in force?
How often do historical alerts lead to an actual HR process change?
new_work: Maintain the source register and monitor failed feeds.
Check legal status, citations and effective dates.
Review false alarms and missed changes.
Maintain guidance versions and follow up assigned actions.
Preserve time for professional learning beyond generated summaries.

tasks.short: Maintain accurate employment records for approved employee changes.

steps.what: Receive an employment-change request and supporting evidence.
Check required fields, effective dates and consistency with the employee record.
Approve material changes and resolve exceptions before they take effect.
Enter the approved change and effective date in the employee record.
Send payroll-relevant changes and reconcile acknowledgement.
File supporting evidence and close the change case.

tasks.design: Configure effective-dated change forms, validation, approval routing and audit history in the {HCM}. A deterministic integration sends approved payroll fields to the {PAYROLL}, reconciles acknowledgements and routes failures to an exception queue. Restricted evidence links in the {DOCS} complete the record without duplicating sensitive documents.
tasks.previous_blocker: The {HCM} often supports these functions already, but local configuration, approval variants and payroll mappings leave manual gaps.
tasks.enabler_now: Most work can be removed through existing configuration. AI coding mainly reduces the cost of integration mappings, reconciliation and exception handling; no model breakthrough is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Retroactive corrections, overlapping changes, payroll lock periods and disputed approvals need careful handling. Sensitive absence evidence requires narrower access than ordinary employee data.
tasks.human_edge: Identify when a requested record change is unsupported, disputed or inconsistent with the employee's actual circumstances.

ambition.what: A weekly review of unresolved employment changes before payroll cutoff.

tasks.altitude: The specialist moves from routine entry to a smaller queue of dated exceptions and corrections. They can prioritise cases by payroll impact; authority to approve employment terms does not increase.

reach.task: Reconcile effective-dated HR changes with payroll inputs.
reach.learn: Payroll cutoffs, retroactive corrections and acknowledgement controls.
Evidence requirements, field validation and restricted-document handling.

build_days.consent_and_access: 10-25; 20-45 where national rules require employee consultation

evidence.claim: Effective-dated records, field validation, approval routing and audit history are established HCM capabilities.
Structured employee-record maintenance generally needs configuration and integration rather than a language-model loop.
GDPR requirements apply to employee records, with additional protection required for health data.
The digest supplies no documented implementation case or measured savings for this record-maintenance design.

assumptions: The typical starting point is the {HCM}; mail bridges the payroll handoff where integration is incomplete.
Requests contain structured fields; reading narrative evidence remains exception work.
Material changes require approval unless valid approval is already attached.
Approved hiring records can arrive from hire-to-productive without repeating contract approval.
Event-specific cases can branch into absence-to-return or offboarding while sharing the same record controls.
All time shares, remaining-time percentages and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Existing effective-dating and approval capabilities in the {HCM}.
Current payroll integration coverage and acknowledgement format.
Which changes require approval and who has delegated authority.
Volume of retroactive, overlapping and disputed changes.
Retention rules, access restrictions and consultation obligations.
research_questions: Which manual entries can existing configuration already remove?
Can changes be replayed safely without duplicate payroll effects?
How are rejected changes, reversals and payroll lock periods handled?
Which evidence can be linked rather than copied between systems?
new_work: Resolve rejected changes and missing acknowledgements.
Maintain mappings, approval routing and validation rules.
Reconcile changes across payroll cutoff dates.
Review access permissions and retention exceptions.
Sample audit trails and test reversal procedures after system changes.

role.altitude: The HR specialist spends less time searching, drafting standard documents and copying records. More time goes to sensitive advice, hiring conversations, legal interpretation and exceptions; additional decision rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Payroll and Timekeeping Clerks: reconcile starter and employment-change data before payroll cutoff.
Labor Relations Specialists: recognise collective agreement issues behind individual questions.
Equal Opportunity Representatives and Officers: assess accessibility and unequal treatment in HR processes.
Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists: assess offer exceptions against job levels and pay ranges.
skills_to_grow: Configure forms, approvals and effective-dated HR records.
Specify integration mappings and reconciliation controls.
Verify cited explanations against current authoritative sources.
Assess equality, privacy and employment implications.
Handle sensitive conversations and negotiate within delegated authority.
Measure exception rates, rework and employee understanding.
role.ambitious_version: Provide an early HR readiness service: review upcoming starters, unresolved employment changes and consequential policy updates together, then bring named risks and practical recommendations to the responsible manager before deadlines.
